name: Ornith-1.5-122B
context_scaling: Native 262,144. The card recommends YaRN factor 4.0 (applied at serve time via rope_scaling override, original_max_position_embeddings 262144) to reach roughly 1M tokens; nothing beyond 262,144 is nameplate.
activation: silu (SwiGLU; sigmoid-routed top-8 of 256 experts plus one always-on shared expert per layer)
attention_variant: Qwen3.5-style hybrid: 36 of 48 layers are gated linear attention (conv kernel 4, 16 key heads x 128, 64 value heads x 128, fp32 SSM state) and 12 are full GQA attention (2 kv heads, head_dim 256, partial rotary 0.25, mRoPE [11,11,10]); full-attention layers at indices 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 27, 31, 35, 39, 43, 47. Adds a 27-block 1152-dim vision tower, so it also accepts images/video (image_token_id 248056).
notes: Released 2026-10-16 under MIT (HF API createdAt 2026-10-16; repo created same day). Nameplate 122B; HF safetensors metadata reports 125,086,497,008 params, recorded as params_b 125.1. HARDWARE FIT: 125.1B x 0.5 GiB = 62.6 GiB of BF16 weights, under the 128 GiB bar, and active params are order 9B, so this is an offload-friendly MoE for a low-VRAM/high-RAM box (weights resident in RAM, 8 of 256 experts routed per token = 3.1% of experts touched per token). ACTIVE PARAMS ARE DERIVED, NOT PRINTED: the card never states an active count. Derivation from config.json: routed expert params = 48 layers x 256 experts x 3 x 3072 x 1024 = 115.96B, so 8/256 routed = 3.62B; shared expert = 48 x 3 x 3072 x 1024 = 0.45B; attention = 12 full layers x (q 3072x16384 gated + k/v 3072x512 + o 8192x3072) ~ 0.94B + 36 linear layers x (in_proj 3072x12288 + out_proj 8192x3072) ~ 2.27B = 3.21B; embeddings 248320x3072 x2 untied = 1.53B; vision tower ~0.45B. Total ~9.3B (text-only path ~8.8B). flops_per_token_active = 2 x 9.3e9, the schema approximation. KV: only the 12 full-attention layers grow with context, 12 x 2 kv heads x 256 head_dim x 2 (K,V) x 2 bytes = 24,576 B/token = 24 KiB/token, i.e. 6.0 GiB at the 262,144 nameplate; the 36 linear-attention layers hold a CONSTANT fp32 state of 36 x (16x128 + 64x128) x 4 B = 1.47 MB per sequence, so this is a bounded-state hybrid with residual KV, not a zero-KV model. SIZE-CLASS UPSET (all vendor-run, single table on this card): 125B beats Beam 501B-A23B on SWE-bench Pro 76.9 vs 57.0, CyberGym 80.0 vs 59.0, NL2Repo 51.2 vs 49.4 and TerminalBench 2.1 81.2 vs 80.1; beats DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (284B) on CyberGym 80.0 vs 76.7 and MCP-Atlas 74.6 vs 74.6 (tie); beats tracked Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B) on 12 of 14 rows (SWE-bench Pro 76.9 vs 43.9, SWE-bench Verified 84.5 vs 82.8, CyberGym 80.0 vs 78.0, SciCode 53.8 vs 47.5). IT LOSES TerminalBench 2.1 81.2 vs 83.4 and Toolathlon-Verified 70.8 vs 71.4 to Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and NL2Repo 51.2 vs 54.2, BrowseComp 78.5 vs 80.2, HLE-with-tools 48.0 vs 50.8 to DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Caveats a reader needs: the table is vendor-only (no third-party row), SWE-bench rows are labelled 'no-hack'/'non-hack' with the card's own anti-reward-hacking instructions, and comparison cells were not re-run by this repo, so cross-column comparability is assumed, not verified. TerminalBench, CyberGym, HLE, SciCode, WideSearch, BrowseComp, MCP-Atlas and Toolathlon have no harness/temperature footnote. The 'runs on a single DGX' line is unquantified (250 GB of BF16 weights). First-party GGUF, FP8, NVFP4 and MLX builds already exist (ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-122B-GGUF, -FP8, -NVFP4, -MLX-4bit/-8bit), plus unsloth GGUF.
